nodes.description: In Satb1-null mice, secretory ameloblasts lose Tomes' processes, apical actin organization and inter-ameloblast adhesion, retain amelogenin intracellularly, and deposit a thin layer of hypomineralized, non-prismatic enamel. SATB1-dependent Eps8 expression is implicated in forming the apical secretory protrusion. Whether the same cellular defect underlies the dental anomalies of patients with CUT-domain missense variants is untested.

nodes.description: Heterozygous missense variants clustered in the CUT1 and CUT2 DNA-binding domains of SATB1 make the protein bind chromatin more strongly than wild-type SATB1 in cell-based assays. Because the variant protein is present and more active rather than absent, this is an altered/increased function mechanism, unlike the haploinsufficiency that underlies the milder allelic DEFDA.
